name: dusty packed wasteland earth ground, a seamless 4x4-tile field with soft tonal patches, long dry cracks and pebbles running across tile borders, mixed with tiles of dry grass tufts
label: wasteland_ruins/dirt-d

surfaces.part: ground field (full 96x80 tile block of packed earth, cracks, pebbles, grass tufts)

answer.evidence: This is a seamless terrain field and not a standing object. The silhouette is a full rectangle with a constant width of 96 across rows 0-79. The column scans show only mottled tonal patches, thin dark crack lines (for example rows 20-24 and 43-44), pebbles with light pixels (rows 7, 39-40 and 55-56) and small yellow grass tufts. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse, no roof plane and no vertical face. It does not read as a standing body, so the top-surface and front-face rules do not apply, and the terrain kind matches the object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows 7 visible tones per 16x16 tile. That matches the paving reference (7) and is well above the grass reference (3). Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as both references, and the picture shows no large single-colour areas. The soil carries about 6 lightness steps, from pale dusty patches through mid browns to dark brown cracks. Speckle grain, small light pebbles with shadow dots, and long cracks that cross tile borders give varied texture throughout. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, and the crack and pebble edges lean visibly brown, so the outline is a dark tone of the neighbouring earth rather than a black sticker line. There is no uniform outline around shapes, and forms are separated by value. The total palette is small (12 colours), but it still produces visible variation at the same density as the references. The dry grass tufts and yellow flecks add some variety. A careful artist would accept this next to the references without it looking thinner or flatter.
